headline: Weekend Brief: Markets looked to oil and upcoming US inflation data as US–Iran tensions lifted crude into a holiday‑shortened week
raw_text:
- US equity futures were little changed after Friday’s mixed close, with US cash markets shut Monday for Labor Day ahead of Tuesday’s reopen
- August US nonfarm payrolls rose 162K versus roughly 55K expected, increasing odds of a possible September Fed rate hike and fueling bond‑market volatility that pressured rate‑sensitive sectors
- Escalating US–Iran tensions and Strait of Hormuz disruptions over the weekend pushed oil (@CL) prices higher, while OPEC+ kept October production quotas unchanged, a setup that could support energy names such as XLE (XLE)
- Higher crude prices and Middle East risk raised fresh inflation concerns that could weigh on energy‑sensitive sectors and keep upward pressure on bond yields
- Asian markets were set to open firmer Monday, with Hong Kong up about 1.7% and South Korea and Japan modestly higher on a tech rebound tempered by geopolitical and yield worries
- Traders planned to monitor global commodity moves and any further Strait of Hormuz developments during Monday’s US market closure
- Key US inflation releases are due later in the week, with PPI scheduled for Thursday and CPI for Friday, providing crucial input on the Fed rate path
- Earnings catalysts for the week include reports from Casey’s General Stores (CASY) early in the week and Oracle (ORCL) and Adobe (ADBE) on Thursday
